To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we show that purified DNAs of spindle‐ and round‐shaped halophilic archaeal viruses transfect haloarchaeal cells, and we use transposon mutagensis to map non‐essential regions in the viral genome.
we have demonstrated the first transfection and transposition mutagenesis experiments in archaeal viruses.
the DNAs of two haloarchaea can transfect haloarchaeal host cells, and that transposon mutagens can be used to identify non‐ essential regions in these viral genomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of tools and techniques that are essential for the genetic analysis of archaeal viruses.
the molecular and cellular biology of viruses of the archaeal domain, and in particular with the ecology and evolution of viruses of the haloarchaea.
the molecular biology of viruses that infect halophilic Archaea.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study demonstrates that haloarchaea can be genetically engineered and that the genomes of spindle and round haloarchaeal viruses are amenable to transposon mutational analysis, and that the results obtained from such analyses are consistent with the current understanding of the molecular biology of these viruses.
this work has provided the foundation for future genetic analyses of halophilic archaeal viruses.
the transfection of haloarchaeon cells by haloarchaeal viral DNA is a feasible approach to genetic manipulation of these viruses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a transfection and mutagenesis system for haloarchaeal viruses, and have identified non‐essential regions of the His2 genome.
haloarchaea can be transduced by the DNAs from spindle‐shaped His2 and round‐shaped SH1, and that transposon mutagensis is a useful technique to identify non‐functional regions of the genomes.
haloarchaeal viruses can transfect a wide variety of haloarchaeon species, and transposons can be used to map genes in the haloarchaeal viral genome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNAs of His2 and SH1 are readily transfected, and can be used for genetic studies.
haloarchaeal viruses are amenable to molecular genetic analysis.
haloarchaeal cytoplasms possess the necessary factors for viral DNA replication and packaging.
